$comment: Explicit, checked-in record of optional capabilities (spec/manifest.json's optional_capabilities) that the bounded C++ host does not yet declare `supported`. Read by tools/spec_runner/host_parity_gate.py. Each entry's `capability` must be a name from spec/manifest.json's optional_capabilities list and must include reason, tracking_issue, affected_host, affected_tests, and removal_condition. An optional capability the C++ host declares `unsupported` (or does not declare at all) that is NOT listed here fails the host-parity CI gate as an undocumented gap. An entry here whose capability the C++ host now declares `supported` also fails the gate (a stale entry) until this file is updated. This file makes no portable-semantics claim of its own -- see docs/releases/R24.md and docs/releases/R25.md for the authoritative evidence it summarizes.

gaps.reason: R27 HTTP serving is not implemented by the bounded R24/R25 C++ host.
gaps.removal_condition: Remove when genia-cpp declares http_server supported and the host parity gate reports the capability as PARITY_OK.

gaps.reason: R14/R27 outbound HTTP is not implemented by the bounded R24/R25 C++ host.
affected_tests: HTTP outbound transport requires-gated shared specs
gaps.removal_condition: Remove when genia-cpp declares http_outbound_transport supported and the host parity gate reports the capability as PARITY_OK.

gaps.reason: Host interop is not implemented by the bounded R24/R25 C++ host.

gaps.reason: docs/design/r26-cpp-data-bridge-contract.md section 5 decided compatibility JSON (json_parse/json_stringify/json_pretty) and parse_jsonl_record are NOT portable and remain Python-host-only, so their previously-ungated shared cases are now retro-gated behind this capability. This is a permanent host-local classification by design, not an in-progress gap awaiting C++ implementation, unless a future contract revision explicitly makes compatibility JSON portable.
gaps.removal_condition: Not expected to be removed by C++ implementation, since this capability is decided Python-host-only by contract. Remove only if a future contract revision makes compatibility JSON portable, genia-cpp then declares json_compat supported, and the host parity gate reports the capability as PARITY_OK.
